verses.text: “There’s a mine for silver and a place where people refine gold.
Iron comes out of the earth, and copper is smelted from ore.
People push back the darkness. They search to its farthest limits for stones deep in the dark.
They cut a shaft far from where people live, where no feet pass. Far from everyone, they hang there and swing back and forth.
Food comes up from the earth, but underneath, the ground is churned up as if by fire.
Its rocks yield sapphires, and its dust holds gold.
No bird of prey knows that path. Even a falcon’s eye hasn’t seen it.
Proud animals haven’t stepped there, and no fierce lion has passed that way.
People put their hands to flint and overturn mountains at the roots.
They cut channels through rock, and their eyes spot every precious thing.
They dam up streams so they don’t trickle through. They bring what’s hidden out into the light.
“But where do you find wisdom? Where does understanding live?
People don’t know its price, and you won’t find it in the land of the living.
The deep says, ‘It isn’t in me.’ The sea says, ‘It isn’t with me.’
You can’t buy it with gold or weigh out silver to pay for it.
You can’t put a price on it in gold from Ophir, precious onyx, or sapphire.
Gold and glass can’t match it. You can’t trade fine gold jewelry for it.
Coral and crystal aren’t even worth bringing up. Wisdom is worth more than rubies.
Topaz from Ethiopia can’t match it, and pure gold can’t measure its worth.
So where does wisdom come from? Where does understanding live?
It’s hidden from the eyes of every living thing, even from the birds in the sky.
Destruction and Death say, ‘We’ve heard a rumor about it.’
“God knows the way to wisdom, and he knows where it lives.
He looks to the ends of the earth and sees everything under the sky.
He set the strength of the wind and measured out the waters.
When he made a decree for the rain and laid out a path for the lightning that comes with thunder,
he saw wisdom and made it known. He established it and searched it out.
He told humanity, ‘Look, wisdom is fearing the Lord. Understanding is turning away from evil.’”
